input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer, failing the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and incapable of fitting the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) because it is a payment-delay charge, not a termination fee. At fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay it is triggered by a minor breach and would exceed remaining contract value within weeks, i.e. walk-away territory. Termination (Sections 9.4 and 10) contains no Customer-payable minimum or early-termination sums, and the SLA credits running to us are beneficial and not flagged. The redline makes the minimal operative change: it flips the operator so no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer, leaving the negated mechanics and the rest of Section 7 (including the interest treatment in 7.3) untouched.

ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages or penalty, including any amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, so we have flipped 7.7 into a prohibition and removed the 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week charge; Vendor's other remedies and the interest treatment in Section 7.3 are untouched.
proposal.summary: Flip Section 7.7 so no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer

mappings.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer.
